status: Whole-group decision: A retained; B/C/D excluded from the current campaign by user instruction. Scoped witnesses are preserved for reconsideration; inverse directions remain separate route requirements.
definition: An internal Workspace has a neighbor on each side. In the 212-route graph its two neighbors must be WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP and CONVERSATION. Orient each whole route around that bridge solely to define membership-side and conversation-side arms. Both root orientations belong to the same structural group.
guards: Reverse-direction routes are grouped for the same inclusion-policy discussion, not declared semantically equivalent or credited as duplicate coverage.

The group definitions use relationship roles and whether a person is terminal or an intermediate join; they impose no maximum edge count. Group A itself includes five-edge routes while other groups include shorter routes.
Examples use explicitly bounded audit channels/roster contacts. IDs must be supplied or discoverable from channel members/messages; histories and member lists are paginated and readable.
Every workspace-membership association is restricted explicitly to the workspace and owner/admin role actually shown by users.info. There is no all-memberships or primary-workspace assertion.

Workspace identities can be exposed; actual stored workspace names are not. Nothing in these groups certifies all terminal fields: last-login, join time, reaction time, complete membership role and stored workspace metadata remain capability-limitation subjects.
Names/content/emoji/counts are representative available selectors. Alternative member-count representations are aliases, not extra groups.
Known anchors bound the candidate population; they must not supply the focal answer or make the bridge constant across every candidate.
Ordinary-request usefulness is the user decision these groups support; a mechanically verbalizable witness alone does not settle that decision.

A.label: Direct workspace connection
A.pattern: Canonical arms: membership side is [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP] or [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP,USER]. Conversation side stays within the conversation and its messages/reactions/memberships, optionally ending at their directly associated USER; it does not continue from that USER to another relation.
A.meaning: Join the profile-shown workspace association to a channel or its contained records/direct participants. A participant may be the channel member, message author or reaction contributor. Identifying that participant is part of the connection; following another relation from that participant is not in this group.

examples.fragment: Audit channels in the workspace shown on the profile of the roster person named Alex.
Review-roster people and their profile-shown workspaces, where that workspace contains an audit-channel message reacted to by someone named Alex.

B.label: Affiliated person’s channel memberships
B.pattern: Canonical membership arm starts [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP,USER,CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP]. Conversation arm is [CONVERSATION], [CONVERSATION,MESSAGE], or [CONVERSATION,MESSAGE,REACTION].
B.meaning: Connect a person’s channel memberships to channels/content in the workspace shown on that person’s profile. The membership can be in the same or a different channel; neither equality nor difference is implied.

examples.fragment: Audit channels in the profile-shown workspaces of roster people who belong to at least three audit channels.
Audit-channel membership entries for roster people whose profile-shown workspace contains an audit-channel message with a thumbs-up.

C.label: Affiliated person’s message or reaction activity
C.pattern: Canonical membership arm starts [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP,USER,MESSAGE] or [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP,USER,REACTION], with its permitted remaining message/reaction extension. Conversation arm stays at [CONVERSATION], [CONVERSATION,CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP], or [CONVERSATION,MESSAGE], as permitted by the no-repeated-type source enumeration.
C.meaning: Connect a person’s authored-message/reaction activity to channels or content in that person’s profile-shown workspace. The activity itself need not occur in that workspace; no extra equality is assumed.

examples.fragment: Audit channels in the profile-shown workspaces of roster people who posted about launch in the audit histories.
Member entries for audit channels whose workspace appears on the profile of a roster person whose audit-history post received a thumbs-up.

D.label: Channel participant’s additional memberships or activity
D.pattern: Canonical membership arm is [WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP]. Conversation arm reaches USER through CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP, MESSAGE authorship, or MESSAGE→REACTION contribution, then continues from that USER to at least one further MESSAGE, REACTION, or CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP relation.
D.meaning: Connect a profile-shown workspace association to one of that workspace’s channels, identify a channel participant/author/reactor, and then use a separate membership or activity of that same participant. Unlike group A, the participant is an intermediate join variable, not the endpoint.

examples.fragment: Review-roster people and their profile-shown workspaces, where that workspace has an audit channel including someone who posted about launch in the audit histories.
Review-roster people and their profile-shown workspaces, where that workspace contains an audit-channel message reacted to by someone belonging to at least three audit channels.
